A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OraPO work and retain matching methods and experiments. All 11 pages of v1 and 17 pages of v2 were readable, including figures, equations, references and v2's supplementary Sections A–C. v1 contains no separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original CheXpert Plus experiments, component and training-size ablations, and training-dynamics results in Tables 1–3 and Figure 2.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds MIMIC-CXR results, expert-label evaluation, an additional ablation, and qualitative results in the supplementary material.

M1.justification: The policy backbone, ZRR-controlled GRPO/DPO mixture, FactS reward and length-aware variants remain unchanged. Supplementary Algorithm 1 adds procedural documentation; it does not establish that the underlying method was revised.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates the proposed method only on CheXpert Plus. v2 adds separate training and evaluation on MIMIC-CXR, previously mentioned only as background, substantially broadening dataset coverage within chest X-ray report generation.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in CheXpert Plus Tables 1–2 are retained. New comparisons introduce methods including CXR-RePaiR, HERGen and MCA-RG in Table 3, MedRAT and other methods in Table 7, GPT-4.1 and GPT-5 Thinking in Table 5, and a GRPO+SFT control in Table 4.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation on 200 studies from 200 patients using three radiologists' majority-vote labels. Commercial-model comparisons use matched images and prompts, with GPT-5 set to medium reasoning. Supplementary evaluations introduce micro-averaged metrics and case-level ROUGE-L. The original CheXpert Plus macro-averaging protocol is retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds an ablation replacing DPO with SFT, checks whether gains persist against expert labels, and presents three qualitative cases with extracted facts, diagnostic discrepancies and ROUGE-L scores. The original component, training-size and training-dynamics analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for its experimental results. The additional evaluations do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the five original ablation rows retain their scores, including CheXpert Plus F1 of 0.341. v2 newly reports MIMIC-CXR macro F1 of 0.357 and micro F1 of 0.481, expert-label F1 of 0.288 versus GPT-5's 0.301, and GRPO+SFT F1 of 0.106. It also adds qualitative scores and inference-time results; these are additional evaluations, not improvements under the original setting.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and objectives in Equations 1–15 are unchanged. Neither version provides formal theorems or proofs, and the new pseudocode and metric explanations do not introduce a new mathematical result.

C1.justification: The abstract extends the headline state-of-the-art claim from CheXpert Plus to MIMIC-CXR, and the contribution summary explicitly emphasizes recall. The central claims of novel GRPO/DPO integration, factual rewards and highly data-efficient training remain the same.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for GRPO+SFT failure, interpretations of expert-label and commercial-model comparisons, and discussion of micro-F1 versus recall. Appendix C argues that low ROUGE-L reflects wording differences rather than clinical errors and interprets individual cases. The original limitations concerning scale, non-verifiable rewards and diagnostic attributes remain in the condensed conclusion.

D1.justification: Appendix A and Table 6 newly disclose the learning rate of 2.5e-7 and hyperparameter search ranges; Algorithm 1 adds pseudocode. Hardware, software, batch/group sizes, mixing settings and length-aware variants were already documented in v1 and are retained or relocated. These disclosures do not establish changed training settings.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands cited coverage of RRG comparators, commercial models, fine-tuning instability and the clinical consequences of missed findings. It also adds newer preference-optimization literature. The original positioning around GRPO, DPO and FactScore, including the claimed first integration, is retained.

P1.justification: The main narrative and method exposition remain largely intact. Local revisions condense contributions, baseline descriptions and the conclusion, while implementation details move into the new supplement and experiments gain subsections. Appendix C also contains an unremoved editorial drafting sentence.

P2.justification: v2 adds four tables, a full-width algorithm display and Figure 3's illustrated qualitative comparison. The former ablation Table 3 becomes Table 4 and replaces its OraPO column with separate GRPO, DPO and SFT columns. Figures 1–2 retain their substantive visual content, with placement and caption adjustments.

improvement.justification: The second-dataset results, expert-label evaluation and SFT control strengthen evidence beyond v1's single-dataset evaluation, while added implementation details aid reproduction. Reporting problems limit the net gain: Table 7 labels scores micro-averaged although MedRAT's precision/recall imply F1 about 0.275 rather than the reported 0.227. Appendix C also overstates factual agreement despite Figure 3's temporal and localization discrepancies. Overall, validation improves, but the additions require more careful reporting and interpretation.
